mainTopic: חדש and the מן at the entry into the land, the dates of משה's death and birth, and which land-based מצוות apply outside ארץ ישראל
overview: The גמרא finishes discussing whether the ban on חדש (new grain before the עומר) applies only in ארץ ישראל after it was conquered and settled, or everywhere. Under the first view, the Jews waited to eat the grain of the land because it was forbidden until the עומר. Under the second view, they waited only because they still had מן. A ברייתא proves this from a פסוק that seems to contradict itself: the מן stopped falling when משה died on the seventh of אדר, but they ate the leftovers until the sixteenth of ניסן. A second ברייתא explains the 'forty years' of מן: the מצות from מצרים tasted like מן. A third ברייתא proves that משה died on the seventh of אדר by counting back 33 days from the crossing of the ירדן. It shows from the extra word 'today' that he was also born on that date. Finally, רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that חדש, כלאים and ערלה apply even outside the land. He proves it with a קל וחומר from חדש. His son רבי אלעזר then begins his own opinion, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: They brought the עומר first and then ate
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the explanation for the view that חדש is forbidden everywhere: the Jews waited, brought the עומר, and only then ate the new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the עומר offering, and only after that did they eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started just before this point. It explains that, according to the first view, the Jews held back from the new grain until they had brought the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יהושע says the Jews ate the grain of the land 'on the day after פסח', meaning not before. According to the view that חדש is forbidden everywhere, this makes sense: the grain was forbidden until the עומר was brought on the sixteenth of ניסן. So the delay is explained by the law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן; it permits the new grain
They brought near, meaning they offered as a קרבן

phrases.english: They offered the omer, and afterward they ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer for the first view, which began before this point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the delay as a legal requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Why did the Jews wait to eat the grain of the land?
steps.terutzMaskana: Under this view, חדש was already forbidden, so they had to bring the עומר first.

steps.title: According to the second view, why didn't they eat right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that חדש only starts after conquest and settlement: if so, the Jews should have eaten the new grain immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the ban on חדש starts only after the land is conquered and settled, they should have eaten immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second view and challenges it. If the ban was not yet in force when they entered, why did they wait until after פסח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, the ban on חדש begins only after ירושה וישיבה, which took fourteen years. On the day they entered the land, nothing stopped them from eating the new grain. So the פסוק's wording that they ate only 'on the day after פסח' looks hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְאַחַר יְרוּשָּׁה וִישִׁיבָה נֵיכוֹל לְאַלְתַּר

steps.kashyaTarget: The view that חדש applies only after ירושה וישיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ban was not yet in force, there was no reason to delay eating the new grain until after the עומר.

steps.title: They did not need the new grain
steps.stepSummary: The answer: they waited not because the grain was forbidden, but because they had no need for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They didn't need to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in just a few words. The Jews were not forbidden to eat the grain; they simply did not need it yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The delay was practical, not legal. They still had food, so there was no reason to eat the new grain. The next step shows from a פסוק what that food was: the leftover מן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the new grain was forbidden. Under this view it was permitted; they just had other food.

phrases.english: They did not need to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason, not a legal one, for the delay
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The delay must mean the grain was forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grain was permitted, but they had no need for it.

steps.title: The פסוק about eating the מן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק showing that the Jews ate the מן until they came to the land, so they had food.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the children of Israel ate the מן forty years, until they came to a settled land; they ate the מן until they came to the border of the land of כנען.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support its answer. The פסוק shows that the Jews were still eating the מן, which is why they did not need the new grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives two endpoints for eating the מן: 'a settled land' and 'the border of the land of כנען'. These two endpoints seem to clash, and the next step points this out. Solving that clash shows the Jews still had מן after they entered the land.

keyTerms.meaning: The food from heaven the Jews ate in the desert
The border or edge of the land of כנען

phrases.english: as it is written: “And the children of Israel ate the manna

they ate the manna

steps.raayaObject: That the Jews still had food (the מן) when they entered the land

steps.title: The two halves of the פסוק seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא points out that the two endpoints in the פסוק seem to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can't say 'until they came to a settled land,' because it already says 'to the border of the land of כנען.' And you can't say 'to the border of the land of כנען,' because it already says 'until they came to a settled land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the פסוק seems to contradict itself about when the Jews stopped eating the מן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A settled land' means inside ארץ ישראל, so they were still eating מן after they crossed in. 'The border of כנען' means just outside, on the plains of מואב, so they stopped before crossing. Both cannot be true unless the two phrases describe two different things.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר ״עַד בֹּאָם אֶל אֶרֶץ נוֹשָׁבֶת״,
phrases.english: One cannot say “until they came to a settled land,”
as it is already stated: “to the borders of the land of Canaan.”

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר ״אֶל קְצֵה אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן״,
phrases.english: And one cannot say “to the borders of the land of Canaan,”

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: ״עַד בֹּאָם אֶל אֶרֶץ נוֹשָׁבֶת״.
phrases.english: as it is already stated: “until they came to a settled land.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר עַד בֹּאָם אֶל אֶרֶץ נוֹשָׁבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the פסוק just quoted and finds an apparent contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two endpoints given in שמות 16:35
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase places the end inside the land and the other places it at the border, so they seem to contradict.

steps.title: The מן stopped falling, but they ate the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The resolution: the מן stopped falling when משה died, but the Jews ate what was left in their vessels until the sixteenth of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? On the seventh of אדר משה died and the מן stopped falling, and they lived on the מן in their vessels until the sixteenth of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא resolves the contradiction. Each half of the פסוק describes a different stage of the מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The border of כנען' marks when the מן stopped falling: when משה died, before they crossed. 'A settled land' marks when they finished eating the leftovers: the sixteenth of ניסן, after they had entered. This proves that they had food in the land until the עומר, which supports the answer in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do the two fit together?
They lived on, they got by on

steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that חדש started only after ירושה וישיבה, the Jews waited to eat the grain only because they still had leftover מן until the sixteenth of ניסן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer lets the second view explain the פסוק in יהושע without saying the grain was forbidden.

phrases.english: How so?
On the seventh of Adar Moses died
and the manna stopped falling,
and they sustained themselves from the manna in their vessels
until the sixteenth of Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the פסוק into two stages: the falling stops, then the leftovers run out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two endpoints describe the same moment and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The falling stopped at משה's death; the eating continued until the sixteenth of ניסן.

steps.title: They didn't really eat the מן for forty years
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא asks how the פסוק can say 'forty years' when they ate the מן for thirty days less than that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'And the children of Israel ate the מן forty years.' Did they really eat it for forty years? Didn't they eat it for forty years minus thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא raises a different question on the same פסוק. The number 'forty years' seems to be off by thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מן began falling a month after they left מצרים, and they stopped eating it on the sixteenth of ניסן in the fortieth year. So the real total is thirty days short of forty years. The ברייתא asks why the פסוק rounds it up.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:

phrases.aramaic: ״וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָכְלוּ אֶת הַמָּן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה״.
phrases.english: “And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years.”
But did they eat it for forty years?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה חָסֵר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם אָכְלוּ!
phrases.english: But didn't they eat it for forty years less thirty days!
phrases.notes: The מן only started falling about a month after they left מצרים, so those first thirty days are missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָכְלוּ אֶת הַמָּן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא on the same פסוק, now asking about the number of years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The actual time they ate the מן was thirty days short of forty years.

steps.title: The מצות from מצרים tasted like מן
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the cakes the Jews took out of מצרים tasted like מן, so those thirty days count too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this comes to tell you that in the cakes they took out of מצרים, they tasted the taste of מן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The first thirty days also count as 'eating מן', because the מצות from מצרים had the taste of מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's 'forty years' is exact, not rounded. The missing thirty days are filled in by the cakes from מצרים, which tasted like מן. So the Jews had a taste of מן for the full forty years.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this comes to tell you

steps.whatToRemember: The 'forty years' of מן includes the first thirty days, when the cakes from מצרים tasted like מן.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:
the cakes that they took out from Egypt,
they tasted in them the taste of manna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets what counts as 'eating the מן'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forty years' is inaccurate by thirty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first thirty days count, because the cakes from מצרים tasted like מן.

steps.title: משה died and was born on the seventh of אדר
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא states that משה died on ז׳ אדר and was also born on ז׳ אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: משה died on the seventh of אדר, and he was born on the seventh of אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives the exact date of משה's death and birth. The next steps will prove each date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 6) we learned that the מן stopped falling when משה died, so the date of his death fits into this discussion. This ברייתא adds a striking claim: he died on his birthday. It states both facts first and proves them one at a time afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: On the seventh of the month אדר

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
On the seventh of Adar Moshe died,
and on the seventh of Adar he was born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of when the מן stopped (at משה's death) by giving the exact date he died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה died on ז׳ אדר and was born on ז׳ אדר.

steps.title: How do we know משה died on the seventh of אדר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that משה died on ז׳ אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that he died on the seventh of אדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how we know the death date. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה never directly says what day משה died. So the date has to be worked out from other פסוקים, and the ברייתא is about to show how.

phrases.english: From where do we know that he died on the seventh of Adar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first half of the claim in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק-based source for משה's death date.

steps.title: Lining up the verses from משה's death to crossing the Jordan
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא strings together פסוקים: משה died, the Jews mourned 30 days, יהושע was told to get ready to cross the ירדן in 3 days, and they came up from the ירדן on י׳ ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'So משה the servant of ה׳ died there,' and it is written: 'The children of Israel wept for משה in the plains of מואב thirty days.' And it is written: 'After the death of משה the servant of ה׳,' and: 'משה My servant is dead; now get up and cross.' And: 'Pass through the camp and command the people: Prepare food, for in three more days you will cross the ירדן.' And: 'The people came up out of the ירדן on the tenth of the first month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists a chain of פסוקים that takes us step by step from משה's death to the day the Jews crossed the ירדן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain gives two time spans: 30 days of mourning after משה died, then 3 days of getting ready. It also gives a fixed date at the end: the crossing on י׳ ניסן. With a known end date and a known number of days, we can count backward to the day משה died.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written (bringing another פסוק)
The first month, which is ניסן
Thirty days (the mourning period for משה)

steps.raayaObject: That משה died on ז׳ אדר.

steps.title: Counting back 33 days lands on the seventh of אדר
steps.stepSummary: Counting 33 days back from י׳ ניסן (30 days of mourning plus 3 days of preparation) brings us to ז׳ אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Count back thirty-three days from there, and you have learned that משה died on the seventh of אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא does the math. It counts backward from the crossing date and arrives at ז׳ אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 33 days are the 30 days of mourning plus the 3 days of preparation. Subtracting them from י׳ ניסן brings us to ז׳ אדר, which proves the first half of the claim in step 9.

phrases.aramaic: צֵא מֵהֶן שְׁלֹשִׁים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: Count back from there thirty-three days,
phrases.notes: That's the 30 days of mourning plus the 3 days of getting ready, counted back from י׳ ניסן.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁבְּשִׁבְעָה בַּאֲדָר מֵת מֹשֶׁה.
phrases.english: so you have learned that Moshe died on the seventh of Adar.

steps.triggerLanguage: צֵא מֵהֶן שְׁלֹשִׁים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים לְמַפְרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the time spans and end date from step 11 to reach the death date.

steps.title: How do we know משה was born on the seventh of אדר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now asks for the source that משה was born on ז׳ אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that משה was born on the seventh of אדר?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא asks about the second half of its claim, the birth date. This sets up the next proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death date is already proven. The birth date needs its own source, because no פסוק says directly when משה was born.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that Moshe was born on the seventh of Adar?

steps.title: The extra word 'today' in משה's words
steps.stepSummary: משה said, 'I am 120 years old today.' The word 'today' seems unnecessary, so the ברייתא asks why it is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He said to them: I am one hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go out and come in.' The פסוק did not need to say 'today.' So why does it say 'today'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes משה's words on the day he died and points out that the word 'היום' looks extra. This prepares the lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה could have just said 'I am 120 years old.' Adding 'today' hints that he turned exactly 120 on that very day. That means his birthday was the same day as his death day, ז׳ אדר.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק did not need to say this

steps.title: God completes the years of the righteous exactly
steps.stepSummary: The word 'today' teaches that הקב״ה fills out the years of צדיקים to the exact day and month, as the פסוק says, 'I will fill the number of your days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that הקב״ה sits and fills up the years of the righteous, from day to day and from month to month, as it says: 'I will fill the number of your days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the extra word 'today': משה's life was completed to the exact day, so he died on his birthday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the payoff of the extra 'היום'. A צדיק's life is not cut short by even a day; it ends on the very date it started. That is why משה's birthday and death day are both ז׳ אדר, completing the claim of step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: I will fill the number of your days

steps.whatToRemember: משה died and was born on ז׳ אדר. The death date comes from counting 33 days back from the ירדן crossing on י׳ ניסן. The birth date comes from the extra word 'היום', which teaches that ה׳ completes the years of צדיקים exactly.

phrases.english: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits
and fills up the years of the righteous
from day to day and from month to month,
as it says: "I will fill the number of your days."

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וּמְמַלֵּא שְׁנוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why say today' question of step 14 and completes the proof of the birth date.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ completes the lives of צדיקים to the exact day, so משה was born on ז׳ אדר, the same day he died.

steps.title: Three מצוות given on entering the land that apply everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that the Jews were commanded three מצוות when they entered the land, and these apply both in ארץ ישראל and outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: The Jewish people were commanded three מצוות when they entered the land, and they apply both in the land and outside the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story of משה and returns to the topic of מצוות connected to entering the land. It opens a new ברייתא, and the three מצוות have not been named yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you might think a מצוה that started when the Jews entered the land only applies in the land. רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that these three are an exception: they began at entry into the land but apply everywhere. The next lines will explain which ones and why.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that because these מצוות started when the Jews entered the land, they only apply in the land. רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches the opposite, and the next steps give his proof.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
The Jewish people were commanded three מצוות
when they entered the land,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹהֲגוֹת בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: and they apply both in the land and outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about משה's dates and returns to the main topic of מצוות tied to entering the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three מצוות commanded when the Jews entered the land apply both in ארץ ישראל and outside it.

steps.title: Setting up the logic: new grain is a light prohibition yet applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי starts a קל וחומר. חדש is lenient in three ways, yet it applies both in the Land and outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Logic tells us these מצוות should apply everywhere. Look at new grain. Its ban is not permanent. It does not forbid benefit. It can become permitted. And yet it applies both in the Land and outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the first half of a קל וחומר. It lists three ways that חדש is a 'light' prohibition, and points out that it still applies everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is to make חדש look as weak as possible. It lasts only until the עומר is brought. Only eating is forbidden, not benefit. It becomes permitted later. If even this weak prohibition applies outside the Land, a stronger one surely should.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'and it is the law'; here it means 'logic says'
'If even...', the opening word of a קל וחומר
Grain from the new crop, forbidden until the עומר offering
A ban on getting any benefit, not only on eating
A way for the forbidden item to become permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Each line about חדש sounds negative, but the negatives are the point. They show how 'light' חדש is, which makes the קל וחומר stronger.

phrases.english: And it is logical that they should apply [everywhere].
phrases.notes: Literally 'and it is the law that they apply.' He means simple logic leads there.

phrases.english: If new grain,
phrases.notes: חדש is grain from the new crop, which may not be eaten until the עומר offering is brought.

phrases.english: whose prohibition is not a permanent prohibition,
and whose prohibition is not a ban on benefit,
and whose prohibition has a way to become permitted,

phrases.aramaic: נוֹהֵג בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ –
phrases.english: applies both in the Land and outside the Land —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical proof for the claim in step 16 that these מצוות apply outside the Land.
steps.raayaObject: That the three מצוות apply both in ארץ ישראל and outside it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The premise that חדש, a lighter prohibition, applies outside the Land

steps.title: So mixed species, a stricter prohibition, must apply everywhere
steps.stepSummary: כלאים is stricter than חדש in all three ways, so it must certainly apply both in the Land and outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mixed species are banned forever. Benefit from them is banned. They never become permitted. Doesn't logic say they should apply both in the Land and outside it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the קל וחומר. It flips each of the three points and shows that כלאים is stricter on every one, so it must apply everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'not' from חדש becomes a 'yes' for כלאים. Its ban is permanent, it forbids benefit, and it never becomes permitted. If the weaker חדש applies outside the Land, the stronger כלאים surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures of species, here grape-vine mixtures
'Is it not logical?', the closing question of a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: חדש is light on all three points and still applies outside the Land. כלאים is strict on all three, so it applies outside the Land even more.

phrases.english: mixed species, whose prohibition is a permanent prohibition,
and whose prohibition is a ban on benefit,
and whose prohibition can never become permitted —
is it not logical that they should apply
both in the Land and outside the Land?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּנְהֲגוּ בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קל וחומר begun in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כלאים applies both in ארץ ישראל and outside it, by קל וחומר from חדש.

steps.title: ערלה fits the same logic on two of the three points
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning works for ערלה, which is stricter than חדש in two of the three ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to ערלה, using two of the points.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds ערלה to the same קל וחומר. It notes that ערלה matches only two of the three strict points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה is not permanent, because it lasts only for a tree's first years. But benefit from it is forbidden, and it never becomes permitted. Those two points are enough to make it stricter than חדש, so it too applies everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
'With two', meaning two of the three strict points

steps.whatToRemember: All three מצוות from step 16 (חדש, כלאים, ערלה) apply outside the Land. חדש is the base case, and כלאים and ערלה follow from it by קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And the same is true of orla, with two [of the points].
phrases.notes: ערלה is not permanent, but benefit is forbidden and it never becomes permitted. Those are the two points.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the conclusion of step 18 from כלאים to ערלה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ערלה also applies outside the Land, since it is stricter than חדש in two ways.

steps.title: A new opinion begins: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא introduces the opinion of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. His words come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון, says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It introduces a new speaker, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, whose view will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we heard רבי שמעון בן יוחי's view and his קל וחומר. Now his son is about to offer his own position on these מצוות. What he says has not been stated yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second opinion after רבי שמעון בן יוחי's view is complete.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The attribution introducing רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view, which continues past this line.
